# Popover

A non-modal, titled surface anchored to a trigger, holding a small piece of interactive content the reader opened on purpose.

**Not implemented yet.** This page is the *approved intent* — the props API signed off at gate 1 of the build order, before any React exists. Do not import it; there is nothing to import.

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `popover` |
| Family | overlays |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | future / future / future |
| Depends on | — |

## Behavior

A non-modal `role="dialog"` carrying `popover="auto"`, positioned against its trigger with CSS anchor positioning — the same top-layer and anchoring machinery as Menu, including the per-instance anchor name. It moves focus in when opened, does not trap it, and returns it to the trigger on Escape. Proposed primitive: `getPopoverProps` in `packages/primitives/src/popover.ts`, sharing Menu's open/close reporting; it is a proposal, not yet a commitment.

- **Popover, Menu, Dialog and Tooltip are four components because they are four contracts** — A Menu is a list of actions with arrow-key navigation and `role="menu"` — putting a text field in one breaks both. A Dialog is modal: the page goes inert and focus is trapped, which is right for a decision that blocks the task and wrong for a filter you glance at. A Tooltip is never focusable and holds nothing interactive. A Popover is the remaining case: a small, non-modal surface the reader opens on purpose, which may contain anything a short form can — a date range, a colour picker, a share link with a copy button, a help text with a "Learn more" link. Each of these differs in focus behaviour, keyboard contract and ARIA role; one component with modes would be four components wearing one name.
- **Focus moves in on open, is not trapped, and returns to the trigger on Escape** — The reader opened it to use it, so focus goes to the first focusable element, or to `initialFocus` when the first one is the wrong place to start. It is not trapped because the popover is not modal — the page behind it is still live, and Tab past the last control leaves the popover and closes it, the same way Tab leaves a Menu. Escape returns focus to the trigger, because that is where the reader was. Light-dismiss by clicking elsewhere is the exception, as in Menu: the reader chose a new place, and taking focus back would undo it.
- **`title` is required, and is a styled label rather than a heading** — A `role="dialog"` must be named, and a visible title naming it through `aria-labelledby` is the name sighted readers get too. It is not a heading element because a popover is not modal: the page's outline is still live behind it, and the popover cannot know what level it sits under — the reason Notice gives. Dialog can use `<h2>` only because everything behind a modal is inert.
- **It is the touch answer for anything a Tooltip cannot do** — A tooltip does not appear on touch, by design. A popover opens on a tap, a click, Enter or Space — the same activation on every input — so supplementary help that must be reachable on a phone, sometimes called a toggletip, is a Popover with a help-icon trigger.
- **No close button by default, and no scrim** — Escape, clicking elsewhere and tabbing out all close it, and the trigger toggles it — four ways out, all expected for a non-modal overlay. A close button is content the caller can add when the popover holds a form with an explicit Done. A scrim would claim the page is inert, which `theme.scrim`'s contract reserves for modals.
- **Web and native** — Web: a `role="dialog"` element, not `aria-modal`, with the `popover="auto"` attribute and `aria-labelledby` pointing at its title; the trigger receives `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` (deliberately not `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, which screen readers announce inconsistently). React Native has no anchored overlay and no top layer, and a small anchored surface is the wrong shape for a phone anyway. On native it renders through the core `Modal` as a sheet from the block-end edge, with `accessibilityViewIsModal` on iOS and the title as `accessibilityRole="header"` — modal on native because the platform offers no non-modal floating surface that screen readers handle. `placement` is web-only.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trigger` | `ReactElement` | — | The control that opens and closes the popover. |
| `title` | `string` | — | The popover's name, shown at its top. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The content: short text, a link, a few fields. |
| `open?` | `boolean` | — | Whether the popover is showing. Makes the component controlled. |
| `defaultOpen?` | `boolean` | `false` | Starting state for an uncontrolled popover. |
| `onOpenChange?` | `(open: boolean) => void` | — | Called whenever the popover asks to open or close — trigger, Escape, light-dismiss or Tab out. |
| `placement?` | `"block-start" \| "block-end" \| "inline-start" \| "inline-end"` | `"block-end"` | Which side of the trigger the popover prefers. |
| `initialFocus?` | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` | — | The element to focus on open, when the first focusable one is the wrong place to start. |

### `trigger`

```ts
trigger: ReactElement
```

The control that opens and closes the popover.

**Use when**

- A `Button` — including an icon-only help button, which is how a toggletip is built.

**Don't use for**

- A non-interactive element. The trigger must be a real button, or the popover is unreachable by keyboard.
- Putting your own `onClick` on it and expecting to be called. The popover owns that handler; use `onOpenChange`.

**Accessibility** Receives `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. Its own text or `aria-label` names the trigger; `title` names the popover.

### `title`

```ts
title: string
```

The popover's name, shown at its top.

**Use when**

- A noun phrase naming what is inside: "Date range", "Share link".

**Don't use for**

- Repeating the trigger's label word for word when that label is a verb ("Share"). Name the thing, not the action.

**Accessibility** Names the `role="dialog"` through `aria-labelledby`. Rendered as a styled paragraph, never a heading — the page's outline is still live behind a non-modal popover.

### `children`

```ts
children: ReactNode
```

The content: short text, a link, a few fields.

**Use when**

- A filter with two or three controls, a help text with a "Learn more" link, a copyable link.

**Don't use for**

- A list of actions. That is a Menu, with arrow-key navigation this component does not have.
- A long form or a decision that blocks the task. That is a Dialog — modal, with a footer.

**Accessibility** Reached by Tab in document order from wherever focus lands on open. Not trapped.

### `open`

```ts
open?: boolean
```

Whether the popover is showing. Makes the component controlled.

**Use when**

- Opening it from somewhere other than the trigger, or closing it after a submit inside it.

**Don't use for**

- Passing it alongside `defaultOpen`. One of them owns the state.

**Conflicts with** `defaultOpen`

**Accessibility** `aria-expanded` on the trigger follows it.

### `defaultOpen`

```ts
defaultOpen?: boolean = false
```

Starting state for an uncontrolled popover.

**Use when**

- Almost never. A popover open before the reader asked covers what they came to see.

**Don't use for**

- Using it to show a message on load. That is a Notice.

**Conflicts with** `open`

### `onOpenChange`

```ts
onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void
```

Called whenever the popover asks to open or close — trigger, Escape, light-dismiss or Tab out.

**Use when**

- Keeping `open` in step, or saving a filter's draft when it closes.

**Don't use for**

- Refusing to close it. A non-modal surface that will not dismiss is a modal without the semantics.

### `placement`

```ts
placement?: "block-start" | "block-end" | "inline-start" | "inline-end" = "block-end"
```

Which side of the trigger the popover prefers.

**Use when**

- `block-start` for a trigger near the bottom of the viewport.

**Don't use for**

- Using it to keep the popover on screen. Anchor positioning flips it near an edge already.

**Accessibility** Visual only, and logical rather than physical. Web only: on React Native the popover is a sheet from the block-end edge.

### `initialFocus`

```ts
initialFocus?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>
```

The element to focus on open, when the first focusable one is the wrong place to start.

**Use when**

- The input in a popover whose first focusable element is a link in its help text.

**Don't use for**

- Pointing it outside the popover. Focus would leave, and leaving closes it.

**Accessibility** A ref rather than `autoFocus`, for the reason Dialog's contract gives: React's `autoFocus` runs on mount, before the popover is shown and focusable.

## Use cases

### A toggletip: help that has to work on touch

A short explanation beside a field, with a link to more — which a Tooltip cannot hold and would not show on a phone.

```tsx
<Popover
  title="Billing email"
  trigger={
    <Button variant="tertiary" iconOnly aria-label="About billing email">
      <Icon icon={CircleHelp} />
    </Button>
  }
>
  <Text>Invoices and receipts go here, not to your login email.</Text>
  <Link href="/docs/billing">Learn more</Link>
</Popover>
```

Opened by a tap, a click, Enter or Space alike. The link is reachable because focus moves into the popover on open. The trigger's `aria-label` names the button; `title` names the popover.

### A small filter, controlled

Two or three controls that refine a list beside them, applied when the popover closes.

```tsx
<Popover
  title="Status"
  trigger={<Button variant="secondary">Status</Button>}
  open={filtering}
  onOpenChange={setFiltering}
  initialFocus={firstOptionRef}
>
  <RadioGroup label="Status" value={status} onValueChange={setStatus}>
    <Radio ref={firstOptionRef} value="open" label="Open" />
    <Radio value="closed" label="Closed" />
  </RadioGroup>
</Popover>
```

Not a Dialog: the list beside it stays live and visible, which is the point of filtering. Not a Menu: these are fields, not actions.

### Reaching for the wrong component

Rename, Duplicate and Delete for a row.

```tsx
<Popover title="Actions" trigger={<Button variant="tertiary">More</Button>}>
  <Button variant="tertiary">Rename</Button>
  <Button variant="tertiary">Duplicate</Button>
</Popover>
```

Don't. A list of actions is a Menu — arrow keys, typeahead, focus returned after a choice, `role="menu"`. A popover of buttons is a menu with none of that.

## Token recipe

### base

Menu's surface with room for content: the same background, outline, shadow and motion, so every anchored overlay in the system reads as one family, and more padding because it holds text and fields rather than one-line rows.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| background | `theme.bg.surface` |
| color | `theme.fg.primary` |
| border | `border.default solid theme.border.default` |
| box-shadow | `theme.elevation.overlay` |
| border-radius | `radius.container` |
| padding | `space.padding.sm` |
| gap between title and body | `space.stack.xs` |
| font-size | `type.body.size` |
| line-height | `type.body.line-height` |
| max-inline-size | `size.control.lg multiplied by 9, or the viewport less space.padding.lg — a stand-in, see Tooltip's measure gap` |
| gap from the trigger | `space.gap.xs` |
| enter transition | `motion.overlay.duration with motion.easing.enter` |
| exit transition | `motion.overlay.duration with motion.easing.exit` |

### title

The popover's name, styled as a label rather than a heading — see the decisions.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| font-size | `type.body.size` |
| font-weight | `type.label.weight` |
| color | `theme.fg.primary` |
